The Verification Gap: Why Faster Code Needs Slower TrustCoding agents changed how much code you produce in a day, and they did nothing at all for my ability to confirm that the code is correct. This article is about closing that gap. We will go through verification patterns: how to decide which lines to read and which to skip, how to use agents to stress test my own API designs, how to get preview environments and continuous documentation checks for close to free, how to contain the damage when something wrong ships anyway, and why flaky tests stopped being worth tolerating.
Along the way, I break down the architecture of a fully automated software factory that ships production security software with no human code review, and show which parts of it scale down to a single laptop. You will finish with a layered reference architecture, a set of prompt patterns you can grab, and the Azure and GitHub services that implement each layer.
